prompt_en: Create a photorealistic cinematic environmental photograph of a spring-wound Clockpunk eclipse rehearsal inside a midnight civic time tower. An unmistakably adult woman, whose broad appearance cues are guided only by the supplied portrait, is the sole human subject, with long near-black wavy hair, warm brown eyes, softly arched brows, an oval face, and natural rose lips. Wearing a charcoal horologist’s coat threaded with fine watch chains, she turns an oversized brass winding key inside a glass-cased astronomical clock; her hand grips the key and its shaft is visibly inserted. Frame one deep three-quarter cutaway so her face, contact, and machinery remain legible. The entire tower visibly runs on repeated mainsprings, cams, and connected gear trains. In the main clock, one transparent cutaway arc links the wound barrel, coiled mainspring, anchor escapement, and bird-release linkage. The key action visibly releases a palm-sized enamel mechanical bird halfway through an open hinged escapement cage while intermeshing brass gears move. Above it, concentric numbered time dials and a distinct moon-phase disk show eclipse. Beside the clock, a clear diagnostic frame compares the escapement beat against a descending brass plumb weight on a marked timing scale. Below it, a maintenance handoff tray pairs a worn cam plate with its polished replacement and a checked-output token; the worn plate sits loose outside the machine. Behind her, a wall-sized gear train, suspended pocket watches, and horological calibration tools extend the system through the tower. Warm clock lamps and cool moonlight share reflections across brass, glass, skin, and worn fabric; subtle contact shadows and foreground occlusion keep the constructed set physically unified.
